question: Suchý zips vymyslel švajčiarsky inžinier po prechádzke so psom. Zaujalo ho, čo sa psovi zachytilo v srsti. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: burdock burrs stuck to his clothes and dog's fur

extra.why_interesting: Everyone uses 'suchý zips' and has pulled burdock burrs off a sweater, but few connect the two. A player can reason it out from childhood memories of burrs sticking to clothes.
extra.verification_notes: Standard accounts say de Mestral found burdock burrs stuck to his dog's fur and his clothes, which inspired Velcro (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_de_Mestral).

explanation: George de Mestral si ich prezrel pod mikroskopom a zistil, že sú pokryté drobnými háčikmi, ktoré sa zachytia o slučky v srsti. Na presne tomto princípe háčikov a slučiek funguje suchý zips dodnes.

question: Pozrite sa na jazdec zipsu na džínsoch alebo bunde. Veľmi často na ňom nájdete vyrazené tri veľké písmená. Ktoré to sú?
source_excerpt: stamped those letters onto the zippers' pull tabs, and thus YKK became known as the Company's trademark.

extra.why_interesting: Most players have seen these three letters on their jeans or jacket thousands of times without registering them. The answer triggers recognition, and the reveal that one Japanese firm zips up much of the world is the payoff.
extra.verification_notes: YKK (Yoshida Kogyo Kabushikikaisha) is the maker whose letters are stamped on a very large share of zipper pulls, so the question's 'very often' holds; see https://rd.com/?p=305789

explanation: Sú to iniciály japonskej firmy Yoshida Kogyo Kabušiki Kaiša. Vyrába takú veľkú časť zipsov na svete, že ju máte takmer určite aj vo vlastnej skrini.
